page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre. Main text in one column: Latin verse with a section heading, a rule, a second poem heading and verse. A marginal note "Istim" stands at the lower right of the text block. Right and left margins carry only scan edge and show-through.

p.i: Sed quales pote scriptit are Versus, Elumbes puta, flaccidos, vietos, Exsucto ingenij vigore vates. Quas si forte tibi tamen vacabit, Vel lectas semel expolire nugas. Fient carmina quæ fuêre nugæ.

main_text.head: In veros veri Dei cultores.
main_text.p: O Te beatum, quem Dei regens timor, Timere cætera prohibet: Cui, seu procellis voluitur furentibus, Seu placida radit æquora, Pectus nec vlla palpitat formidine, Nec sorte turget profpera: Intentus vni qui placere numini, Prodesse quærit omnibus! Sed tanta tam paucos, rogo, cur amulos Sortitur hæc beatitas?
main_text.head: IN CLEMENTEM PVTEANVM iestæ à Pseudo Iefu cognominatæ patrem, in Dolensi gurgustio.
main_text.p: PVtere tibi qui, Puteane, dicitur Bezæ abnegata veritate perfidus, Velut tumulo iam suo putris iacens, Et siuit, & salet, stultimum iam septima

page.notes: Text partly ornamented; "Istim" is a printed marginal or catchword-like mark at lower right. Several letters in the verse are uncertain (e.g. "Ψ"-like initial and the word "stultimum"); the Greek/ornamental letter forms are rendered approximately. Left margin contains no printed text.
